data.title: Global Compliance Applications Corp. Signs Memorandum of Understanding to Evaluate Blockchain Coupon and Rewards Integration with Instacash in Eswatini
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 9, 2026) - Global Compliance Applications Corp. (FSE: TK6) (OTC Pink: FUAPF) (the "Company" or "GCAC") announces that it has entered into a memorandum of understanding on October 9, 2026 (the "MOU") with Directore Technologies (Proprietary) Limited, trading as Instacash ("Instacash"), to evaluate the integration and potential commercialization of GCAC's coupon, rewards and merchant-engagement technology within Instacash's payment and wallet ecosystem in Eswatini.

The MOU establishes a framework for technical, commercial and regulatory due diligence, pilot design and negotiation of definitive agreements. The proposed technology would support merchant coupons, customer rewards, campaign management and redemption analytics while Instacash would retain control of its 220,000 user customer relationships and regulated payment operations. Any proposed blockchain or digital-asset functionality beyond the coupon record would require separate legal and regulatory analysis.

Proposed Commercial Framework

The parties are evaluating a potential technology deployment package with a stated negotiation value of up to US$1,000,000. This amount is a proposed commercial valuation and is not an agreed payment, booked revenue, financing commitment or independently established asset value. The MOU contemplates that consideration, if agreed, could comprise cash, equity or deferred value, revenue participation, or a combination. No final pricing, payment schedule, equity issuance or revenue-sharing terms have been agreed.

The parties also contemplate a staged pilot, with milestones and acceptance criteria to be agreed in a written pilot plan. Any production rollout would depend on satisfactory technical integration, commercial feasibility, data protection, regulatory review, internal approvals and execution of definitive agreements. The MOU does not obligate either party to complete a production deployment or securities transaction.

"We see an opportunity to evaluate how GCAC's coupon and engagement infrastructure can complement an existing African payments ecosystem of 220,000 plus users without displacing its core payment functions," said Ryan Gibson, Chief Executive Officer of GCAC. "Our immediate priority is a disciplined assessment of the technology, economics and regulatory requirements before committing to a commercial rollout. Our goal, is to provide a lucrative advertising and business stream of revenue for the Payment Operator in the spirit of creating an African based super wallet."

Material Terms and Status

The MOU provides for an initial evaluation period, with a six-month term unless extended or terminated under its provisions. Certain provisions, including confidentiality and specified protections, are intended to be binding; the principal commercial arrangements remain subject to definitive documentation. Any equity consideration would require separate agreements, applicable corporate and regulatory approvals, and CSE acceptance where required. No securities are being issued pursuant to the MOU at this time. There can be no assurance that the proposed pilot, deployment or commercial transaction will proceed.

About Global Compliance Applications Corp.

Global Compliance Applications Corp. develops and licenses blockchain-enabled technology solutions, including its Efixii platform and related digital engagement and data-management applications. For further information, visit the Company's corporate website and public disclosure record. (http://www.gcac.tech).

On behalf of the Board of Directors

data.title: Research Reports — Barrons.com
data.description:
These reports, excerpted and edited by Barron's, were issued recently by investment and research firms. The reports are a sampling of analysts' thinking; they should not be considered the views or recommendations of Barron's. Some of the reports' issuers have provided, or hope to provide, investment-banking or other services to the companies being analyzed.

Chevron — CVX-NYSE Buy — $206 on Oct. 7 by Melius Research Chevron holds the most advanced foreign position in a reopened Venezuela: On Sept. 2, Chevron secured new fiscal terms and two greenfield Orinoco blocks. The plan lifts gross joint-venture production from about 280,OOO barrels a day to about 600,000 barrels a day by 2031 on more than $7 billion of joint-venture investment over five years — at a total cost below $20 a barrel. Stability clauses protect the negotiated royalty and tax through changes of administration, and the contracts carry a right to international arbitration.

Despite political risk in Caracas and Washington, Chevron's position is strong as U.S. policy continues to actively support the expansion. Target price: $241.

Coinbase Global — COIN-Nasdaq Buy — $185.74 on Oct. 7 by BTIG Research & Strategy Coinbase Global shares have rallied more than 25% since the day after second-quarter earnings (July 31) as spot trading volume sequentially improved each month during third-quarter 2026 (per data we track from The Block). The data indicate that Coinbase's spot trading volume during September was the strongest month the company has had since February.

Additionally, Coinbase appears to be a share gainer during the quarter, with spot trading volumes down about 2% quarter over quarter compared with the broader crypto market, down about 7%.

We are lifting our Coinbase third-quarter 2026 revenue estimate by 2.8%, to $1.202 billion (from $1.169 billion) and are now 3.4% above consensus. Target price: $240.

Chewy — CHWY-NYSE Outperform — $18.14 on Oct. 7 by Mizuho Effective on Monday night, Chewy pushed through updates to its still early-stage Chewy+ membership program. We caught up with the company postchange. The main differences for the revamped program include: 1) a price cut to $59 per year from the $79 annual membership fee, which was initially tested at $49 dating back to November of last year; 2) added telehealth benefits and a 10% discount on future visits; and 3) free samples from vendors. We believe that the revised program brings a new baseline of features, with additional ones to be bolted on over time.

Our initial review doesn't screen as a material sales or customer driver just yet. We were looking for something more disruptive and directly appealing to pet owners. The burden of proof still very much remains on Chewy to reaccelerate the top line and break above the mid-single digit percentage core revenue cadence of recent quarters. Target price: $28.

IMAX — IMAX-NYSE Buy — $52.72 on Oct. 6 by Seaport Research Partners IMAX posted third-quarter 2026 box-office results throughout its network of $712 million, which was ahead of our $659 million estimate. Elevated indexing of films continues, among hits like The Odyssey (30%-plus), solid performers like (Resident Evil at 15%), and busts like Digger (18%). We expect a solid fourth-quarter 2026 to finish the year. Target price: $58.

Black Hills — BKH-NYSE Buy — $70.74 on Oct. 7 by Siebert Williams Shank Yesterday, Black Hills announced that it has executed agreements to provide approximately 590 megawatts of generation and other services to a Google data center to be constructed near the company's Cheyenne, Wyo., service area. The company indicated that while the data center is located in the Cheyenne region, it will serve the data center primarily with a new 564 MW nonregulated natural-gas-fired resource, Cheyenne Prairie Generating Station. The company expects the new power plant investment of roughly $1.8 billion and the services agreements to result in annual earnings of approximately $150 million in 2030.

The implications are huge for Black Hills as a stand-alone company....The company's expectations for $150 million of 2030 net income is nearly a 33% increase relative to our prior 2030 Black Hills estimate. Even with conservative assumptions for incremental equity dilution, we estimate that Black Hills' stand-alone earnings-per-share growth rate escalates almost 50% from 6.3% to over 9% through 2030. There are significant implications for balance-sheet improvement and dividend growth, as well. Target price: $91.

Sportradar Group — SRAD-Nasdaq Buy — $12.18 on Oct. 7 by StoneX Equity Research We view Sportradar Group's $170 million cash sale of Atrium Sports as an attractive monetization of a nonstrategic business with limited growth. We estimate annual revenue of approximately $44 million and adjusted Ebitda of $13 million-plus, implying transaction multiples of approximately four times sales and 13 times adjusted Ebitda. The estimated earnings contribution translates to approximately 11.5 million euros-plus, or 3.2% of our EUR360 million 2026 adjusted Ebitda forecast, with the actual fourth-quarter impact dependent on closing timing.

Sportradar retains key technology supporting its core offerings, while sale proceeds and an expected $50 million IMG Arena-related cash payment in November could provide approximately $220 million in combined gross cash inflows to support existing capital allocation priorities, including share repurchases. Target price: $14.

data.title: Boarded windows and evacuations as major hurricane nears US Gulf coast
data.description:
By Andrew Hay

Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing with it life-threatening storm surge and 115 mph (185 kph) winds.

Tens of thousands of people in Florida's Panhandle and Alabama's Gulf Coast faced mandatory evacuation orders. Local television stations showed roads packed with vehicles heading north, away from the water.

The Category 3 Isaias, the first hurricane of an unusually quiet season for the United States, was expected to make landfall between Mobile, Alabama, and Grayton Beach in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening, according to the National Hurricane Center.

The 90-mile (145 km) stretch of coast is known for brilliant-white sand beaches, with some areas packed with vacation homes next to small coastal towns like Destin, Florida.

"If you've been asked to evacuate, get out now, conditions are only going to deteriorate," NHC Director Michael Brennan told Fox Weather on Friday. "That surge is going to come in after dark, that's not a place you are going to want to be in."

Scientists say human-caused climate change has warmed the Gulf of Mexico, possibly intensifying hurricanes like Isaias.

The storm will pack sustained winds capable of extensive structural damage to beach houses, though modern homes built to strict coastal codes may remain standing. Storm surge of up to 9 feet (2.7 meters) was forecast around the Alabama-Florida border.

President Donald Trump canceled a planned trip to Alabama on Saturday for ​the Georgia vs. Alabama college football game, as the hurricane is expected to affect Tuscaloosa, the city where the contest was set to be played.

Up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain was expected in localized areas of the Florida Panhandle and the Big Bend area.

Oil companies have evacuated personnel from 129 oil and gas production platforms, representing 35% of the 371 ​staffed platforms in the Gulf of Mexico.

Hurricane-force winds were expected as far as 100 miles inland in southern Alabama, possibly triggering tornadoes. Some 2 to 5 inches (5 to 13 cm) of rain were expected across the US Southeast as far north as the southern Appalachian Mountains and coastal areas of the Carolinas.

data.title: How to Get a Good Night's Sleep — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Americans have been feasting on debt for far too long ("A Divided Stock Market Looks Scary. It Could Be the Setup for a Serious Rally," Cover Story, Oct. 2). Eventually, the market will correct and the bubble will pop. But no one knows when. I just merrily buy more certificates of deposit, Treasury inflation-protected securities, munis, etc. and stay invested in broad exchange-traded funds with plenty of cash on the sidelines.

We cannot predict, but we can prepare. As John Maynard Keynes famously remarked, "Markets can remain irrational longer than you can remain solvent." I'm 78 years old, so I hold no more than 25% in stocks. I like to sleep at night.

Curtis Turchin On Barrons.com

Blame the Media

To the Editor: What an enlightened and optimistic article! ("Capitalism Is Out of Style. Both Parties Are to Blame," Other Voices, Oct. 2.) It reminded me of a professor who told us that "10% of our Constitution was intended to protect citizens from one another and 90% was to protect citizens from government."

I would add that the media are as much to blame as either political party for capitalism's unpopularity. News media often gloss over absurd and inefficient policies as if they're just part of modern times, then skewer a company that makes its fortune developing and selling a product that improves people's lives.

John Rohde On Barrons.com

The Inflation Effect

To the Editor: Randall W. Forsyth makes many salient points in his discussion of consumer spending ("If Consumers Are So Down on the Economy, Why Are They Spending So Freely?" The Economy, Oct. 2). However, he doesn't mention the inflation effect, which causes people to spend more now because they know prices are going even higher in the future, given the incoherent policies flowing from Washington.

When I go to Costco Wholesale or other stores, I load up on nonperishable items on sale because I know they're only going to get more expensive. Just take a look at aluminum foil prices since the U.S.-Canada trade fiasco reared its ugly head again. Solid sales now may merely be borrowing from future sales.

Steven Morris Mt. Pleasant, S.C.

Micron: Peak to Trough

To the Editor: I'm a longtime Micron Technology holder ("Micron's Stock Is Cheap. Why Investors Are Still Gun-Shy," Tech Trader, Oct. 2). This time of peak/trough transition may indeed be different because of the added importance of high-bandwidth memory, which was nonexistent prior to the explosive growth of data centers. I sold some Micron to recoup losses from Intuit but intend to keep the rest of my shares. Next likely trough: fourth-quarter 2027?

Narayana Mysore On Barrons.com

data.title: Shawn Fain Claims Victory in UAW Election Rout — WSJ
data.description:
By Christopher Otts

United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain and his allies on Friday claimed an easy victory in the union's election, cementing Fain's leadership of one of the most powerful forces in American organized labor.

Fain, known for his profane, confrontational style, secured a position of strength for the union's next showdown with Ford Motor, General Motors and Jeep-Ram parent Stellantis in 2028 over labor contracts. The UAW priorities will include seeking to restore benefits such as traditional pensions and winning protections against artificial intelligence and automation replacing factory jobs.

"The membership has spoken," Fain said Friday. "UAW members are united and want us to keep fighting and building on what we've done."

While official results weren't available, tallies posted by Fain's campaign showed his garnering about 68% of the vote as of Friday afternoon. A UAW spokesman said official results would come later.

UAW Vice President Mike Booth, who ran on a ticket opposing Fain, told The Wall Street Journal that there is no doubt about the outcome.

Fain faced five challengers, including a UAW vice president with whom he had feuded. Fain's allies defeated top UAW officials whom Fain viewed as impediments to his agenda for vice presidential slots and other key roles.

"Fain's got to be very happy about this; it could not have turned out better for him," said Marick Masters, a business professor and labor expert at Wayne State University in Detroit.

Fain had clashed with another UAW vice president, Rich Boyer, who unsuccessfully challenged Fain for the top job. He also feuded with the person who signs the checks for union expenses, Secretary-Treasurer Margaret Mock. Boyer and Mock didn't immediately return a request for comment.

Fain, a former Chrysler plant electrician from Kokomo, Ind., had been a virtually unknown staffer at the union's Detroit headquarters when he narrowly won the top job in a runoff election in 2023. He was part of a hastily arranged "reform" slate meant to steer the union past a corruption scandal that sent two former UAW presidents to federal prison.

It was the first time the storied union allowed its members, rather than a cadre of insiders, to directly vote on its president and top leaders.

Fain, 57 years old, soon became one of the labor movement's most recognizable figures, adopting a more confrontational posture with the Detroit automakers, hurling profanities and wearing "Eat the Rich" T-shirts during speeches.

During contract talks in 2023, Fain called targeted strikes of certain auto plants, such as the Kentucky facility where Ford produces its most profitable trucks. The union secured large wage increases and other gains when the carmakers relented.

Fain's UAW then realized a long-sought goal of organizing a foreign automaker's plant, winning union representation at Volkswagen's factory in Chattanooga, Tenn. But the UAW has been unable to extend its wins to other foreign auto plants.

At the union's home base in Detroit, Fain has been bogged down in internal controversies. A federal monitor charged with overseeing the union accused Fain of retaliating against Mock and Boyer. Fain has had to restore powers he and the board had stripped from his rivals and part ways with his chief of staff and top strategist.

Write to Christopher Otts at christopher.otts@wsj.com

data.title: Nasdaq short interest up about 3% in late September
data.description:
Short interest on the Nasdaq rose 2.99% in late September, the exchange said on Friday.

As of September 30, short interest rose to about 18.657 billion shares, from 18.117 billion shares as of September 15.

Investors who sell securities "short" borrow shares and then sell them, expecting the stock to fall so they can buy the shares back at the lower price, return them to the lender and pocket the difference.

data.title: Alignment Healthcare downgraded at BofA after CMS Star Rating for MA contract
data.description:
BofA Securities on Friday downgraded Alignment Healthcare to Neutral from Buy after CMS lowered its Star Rating for one of its major California Medicare Advantage contracts to 3.5 stars from 4.

The bank lowered its price target to $9 from $25 (~19% upside based on the Oct. 9 close).

BofA noted that Alignment Healthcare went from having all of its members in plans with at least 4 stars to just 25%. The important California contract, H3815, is responsible for 75% of the managed care company's MA membership.

As a result, the contracts with a rating of below 4 stars won't eligible for bonus payment from CMS, which "potentially [makes] it more

difficult to expand profitably into new markets," analyst Kevin Fischbeck said.

"However, there is a potential silver lining, in that if the company can move up its star rating on that one contract, there will be a meaningful lift to profitability in 2029, he added. "We see this as real potential, but visibility remains low and the binary nature of the event likely means that the ALHC stock will trade at a discount to its historical average until we see improvement."

Alignment Healthcare closed down ~13%.

data.title: Trump taps Russia to boost global diesel supplies ahead of midterms. It may be 'too little, too late,' says strategist.
data.description:
By Myra P. Saefong and Victor Reklaitis

Former U.S. ambassador to Russia under Obama calls Trump's U-turn on Russia 'absolutely deplorable'

The U.S. Treasury Dept. has temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

The Trump administration took a U-turn on Friday and enlisted Russia to help boost U.S. and global diesel supplies in an effort to lower prices for the fuel ahead of the fast-approaching U.S. midterm elections in November.

President Donald Trump said in a social-media post on Friday that he made a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin that will lead to Russia supplying more than 300,000 tons of diesel "to the American and Global Marketplace," followed by another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons after that.

Additionally, Russia will then deliver, "within a short period of time," 3 million tons of diesel fuel, Trump said.

"The headline may move prices initially, but this is hardly a straightforward solution," said Rebecca Babin, a senior energy trader and managing director at CIBC Private Wealth.

The U.S. is turning to Russian diesel just after tightening sanctions, which shows the difficult tradeoffs involved in securing supply, she told MarketWatch by email.

For context, the proposed 4.8 million metric tons is roughly 36 million barrels, or 400,000 barrels a day over three months - and delivery depends on refinery availability, said Babin. "Those barrels could help, but they may not fully materialize, and what does arrive will likely still be too little, too late."

Trump, who faces criticism about the elevated cost of living as November's midterm elections get closer, said the deal means diesel prices will fall for Americans. Prices for diesel at the pump had climbed to a record high of $6.528 a gallon on Sept. 22, according to AAA.

After Trump's post, the U.S. Treasury Department said it was "immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market," with that move coming at the president's direction.

Following the news, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on X: "Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world."

"Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," said Zelensky.

Russian energy exports have faced major U.S. sanctions since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022, and three weeks ago Trump signed into law a new Russia sanctions bill named after the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham.

Trump's decision Friday to pause sanctions on Russia drew criticism. A former U.S. ambassador to Russia during the Obama era, Michael McFaul, said the president "not only cut off U.S. military assistance to Ukraine, but he is now providing Putin with new money to build more Russian rockets and drones to kill Ukrainians. Absolutely deplorable."

The United States continues to play a constructive role in speaking to Russia and Ukraine to work toward bringing the war to an end, and is the only country in the world that can play that role, a White House official told MarketWatch on Friday.

Ahead of the news, U.S.-traded West Texas Intermediate (CL.1) and Brent crude futures (BRN00) settled Friday with a gain of 0.4% each. Ultralow-sulfur diesel (HO00), also known as heating oil, fell 3%.

Robert Schroeder contributed.

-Myra P. Saefong -Victor Reklaitis

data.title: Orca Energy Group Provides Update on Songo Songo Licence, Operations, and the Proposed Transaction
data.description:
TORTOLA, British Virgin Islands, Oct. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Orca Energy Group Inc. (“Orca” or the “Company”) (TSX-V: ORC.A, ORC.B) provides an update regarding a proposed extension of the Songo Songo Development Licence (the “Licence”), related operational matters concerning PanAfrican Energy Tanzania Limited (“PAET”), and the Company’s previously announced proposed transaction (the “Proposed Transaction”) involving Taifa Gas Tanzania Limited and Amber Energy Investment L.L.C-FZ (the “Purchasers”). The Company also notes that, on October 5, 2026, the Fair Competition Commission of Tanzania (the “FCC”) issued a notice prohibiting the merger application relating to the Proposed Transaction.

Proposed Licence Extension

On October 1, 2026, the Minister of Energy of Tanzania (the “MoE”) issued a notice of intention to grant an extension of the Licence to the Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (“TPDC”) and PAET, which provided proposed terms and conditions for such an extension. The MoE’s notice contemplates a statutory process under which a response is required within 60 days and states that rights and obligations under the existing Licence and the Production Sharing Agreement (the “PSA”) continue during that process.

On October 9, 2026, PAET responded to TPDC and advised that it rejects the proposed extension terms, on the basis that the proposed commercial and fiscal terms are uneconomic and unacceptable. PAET also advised that its response does not constitute acceptance of the proposed extension terms and that it reserves its rights and remedies under applicable agreements, law and ongoing arbitration proceedings.

Songo Songo Operations

PAET has advised TPDC and the MoE, notwithstanding its rejection of the proposed Licence extension terms, that it is willing to continue operating the Songo Songo facilities under the existing Licence and PSA framework to ensure that gas continues to flow to customers for the duration of the applicable 60-day statutory period in order to support an orderly transition of operations to TPDC and Songas Limited (“Songas”). PAET has proposed the establishment of a transition working group involving PAET, TPDC and Songas to coordinate transition planning and operational readiness activities. PAET has also advised that it intends to cease operating the Songo Songo facilities by November 29, 2026, or earlier if TPDC and Songas confirm operational readiness.

Proposed Transaction

As previously disclosed, Orca entered into a Sale and Purchase Agreement with the Purchasers on April 10, 2026, pursuant to which Orca agreed to sell all of the outstanding shares of PAE PanAfrican Energy Corporation, Orca’s Mauritian holding subsidiary through which Orca indirectly owns PAET. On October 5, 2026, the FCC issued a notice prohibiting the merger application relating to the Proposed Transaction. The FCC's notice provided no additional information regarding how or why the FCC took the decision to prohibit the merger application. The Proposed Transaction has not been terminated. Orca is seeking additional information and analysing the implications of the FCC decision while assessing it's options with respect to the Proposed Transaction and will provide further updates as appropriate.

About Orca Energy Group Inc.

Orca is an international public company engaged in natural gas exploration, development and supply in Tanzania through its subsidiary PanAfrican Energy Tanzania Limited. Orca trades on the TSX Venture Exchange under the trading symbols ORC.A and ORC.B.

data.title: American Express Shares Get a Lift on Delta Friday — WSJ
data.description:
By Ben Glickman

American Express shares ended higher Friday, thanks to a boost from Delta Airlines.

Delta Airlines' third-quarter results said that: New cards and spending on Amex and Delta's co-brand cards each grew over 10%. The carrier expects to receive over $9 billion this year from Amex as part of the two companies' co-branded cards, up from $8.2 billion last year.

That helped Amex investors shrug off a reprimand and fine from regulators.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said it was fining Amex $350 million after it had found Amex's compliance program for financial crimes had been inadequate. That was in part because its program did not properly match the risks in its business and had not been given appropriate resources, regulators said.

Shares opened trading down on Friday about 1%, but closed up 0.3%.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Two Sidus Space directors resign, citing governance disagreements
data.description:
Satellite technology firm Sidus Space said on Friday two directors had resigned from its board, citing disagreements over governance and management practices.

The company said it disagreed with the assertions made by the directors in their resignation letters. Here are some details:

  • Tiffany Norwood and Kelle Wendling resigned from Sidus Space's board effective October 6, according to a regulatory filing.

  • Norwood, chair of the audit committee and a member of the corporate governance and nominating committee, cited "a number of concerns and disagreements", including the handling of a confidential complaint brought to her and other committee chairs.

  • Wendling, a member of the audit, compensation, and corporate governance and nominating committees, said she resigned after considering matters related to the company's management and governance.

  • Sidus Space included both directors' resignation letters in the regulatory filing.

  • "I have previously raised concerns regarding these matters through the appropriate Board and committee processes, and those concerns remain unresolved," Wendling said in her letter.

  • The company said it had notified Norwood and Wendling of its disclosures and given them an opportunity to state whether they agreed with its response.

data.title: Moody's lifts Ghana rating to 'B3' as debt burden eases
data.description:
Moody's lifted Ghana's sovereign rating to "B3" from "Caa1" on Friday, the second upgrade in a year, citing lower borrowing costs and improved debt affordability.

The West African nation, a major producer of gold, oil and cocoa, is recovering from its most severe economic crisis in decades following a debt restructuring and an IMF bailout.

"Financing costs have remained lower despite external headwinds from the Middle East conflict, a reflection of continued fiscal discipline, which is underpinned by institutional improvements," Moody's said.

The agency noted that a key underlying credit support has been an increase in the price of Ghana's exports, which it expects to be sustained.

Ghana, Africa's largest gold producer, is a beneficiary of historically elevated gold prices, with gold accounting for 67% of the country's goods exports in 2025. Moody's expects prices of the metal to support strong current account surpluses.

The credit rating agency revised Ghana's outlook to stable from positive, which it had assigned in April, and said it expected Ghana's macroeconomic stability and reduced government liquidity risk to be sustained.

In May, peer agency Fitch retained Ghana's outlook as "positive" and upgraded its rating to "B", citing fiscal reforms that helped with real GDP growth, while S&P maintained its ratings at "B-/B" with outlook at "stable" in September.

data.title: Verizon, AT&T And T-Mobile Shares Plunge As SpaceX Strikes Spectrum Deal To Expand Starlink Mobile
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Shares of major US telecommunications companies fell sharply on Friday after Elon Musk's SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide wireless spectrum portfolio from private-equity firm Grain Management, strengthening its plans to expand Starlink into mobile services.

Verizon shares dropped around 10 percent, putting them on track for their steepest single-day decline since 2002. T-Mobile fell 13 percent, its worst potential daily performance since 2013, while AT&T lost approximately 10 percent, marking its biggest decline since 2000. SpaceX shares rose around 1 percent.

The deal covers Grain Management's nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz spectrum licences, comprising up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum. The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX would pay approximately $8 billion in cash, although the companies did not disclose the financial terms.

The acquisition could help Starlink Mobile improve connectivity inside buildings and in areas where conventional mobile networks struggle.

Low-band spectrum travels longer distances and penetrates obstacles more effectively than higher-frequency signals, potentially strengthening SpaceX's ability to deliver satellite connectivity directly to standard mobile phones.

The transaction remains subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). FCC Chair Brendan Carr described increased competition in the spectrum market as positive for American consumers, adding that the market would determine which providers succeed.

Analysts at Evercore ISI said the acquisition gives SpaceX the foundations of a more developed network, while JPMorgan said it makes Starlink Mobile's long-term opportunity more credible.

However, analysts cautioned that established wireless carriers face limited near-term risk because building a competitive network requires considerable time, infrastructure and capital.

data.title: Record Diesel Prices Squeeze US Trucking Industry, Threatening Higher Consumer Costs
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Record-high diesel prices are squeezing the US trucking industry, raising transportation costs and increasing the risk of higher consumer prices.

The surge comes as the sector continues recovering from a prolonged freight downturn marked by falling shipping rates, business failures and job losses.

JD & LA Trucking, a family-owned company operating 20 trucks between the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach and regional warehouses, is among those facing mounting expenses.

Co-owner Angel Diaz said diesel prices had risen from just over $5 per gallon earlier this year to $8.38 at some Los Angeles-area stations. He warned that sustained increases could force more trucking companies to close or sell their vehicles.

The industry is also facing a shrinking driver supply following employment losses and federal restrictions affecting certain commercial driving licences. Although freight rates have started recovering, fuel costs are rising faster than carriers can adjust their prices.

The pressure is spreading across supply chains, with transport companies and consumer brands reporting higher fuel and labour expenses. The Food Industry Association estimates diesel price increases can take 30 to 45 days to reach grocery stores.

President Donald Trump recently signed an executive order aimed at easing diesel costs by relaxing certain restrictions on red-dyed diesel, generally reserved for off-road use.

However, industry representatives warn that the measure is unlikely to provide a lasting solution, leaving businesses and consumers exposed to continued cost pressures.

data.title: Gold snaps two-week losing streak; some analysts say may have found bottom
data.description:
Gold futures rose Friday to finish at one-week highs, ‌posting a weekly gain after back-to-back losses, supported by resilient investment demand despite rising U.S. Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.

Elevated bond yields and persistent inflation pressures continue to keep a lid on gold prices, but analysts noted that investors continue to see value in the market as dips continue to be bought.

Despite the risks, this week's price action suggests the gold market may have found its bottom, Forex.com market analyst Fawad Razaqzada said in a note.

"Gold investors are largely seeing through risks of tighter monetary policy because of concerns that inflation may again overshoot due to high oil prices," Razaqzada wrote. "Precious metals are proving their worth as a hedge against inflation, with fiat currencies continuing to lose value across the world due to persistent price pressures. This is reflected in gold-backed ETFs continuing to receive inflows during the recent price decline."

High borrowing costs could ultimately support gold through two scenarios, according to Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen: an economic slowdown that drives yields lower and encourages monetary easing, or rising government debt servicing costs that prompt policy intervention and weaken confidence in monetary discipline.

"Neither outcome is inevitable, and further increases in real yields remain a near-term risk," Hansen said in a note. "Nevertheless, continued ETF accumulation suggests some investors are positioned for the potential consequences of elevated borrowing costs rather than simply responding to current interest-rate movements."

Gold ​gained this week because of "bargain hunting at the lows, as a floor has been building in the $4,000-region," ​StoneX head of market analysis Rhona O'Connell wrote. "It is arguable that a further Fed hike is already priced in but so is the expectation for continued official sector net purchases. Without any Black ​Swan event, I find it hard to see gold breaking convincingly higher."

This week, front-month Comex gold for October delivery gained 1.4% to $4,191.00/oz, its highest settlement value in a week, and front-month Comex October silver added 1.1% to $60.670/oz; on Friday, gold and silver rose 1.4% and 2.7%, respectively.

data.title: Mexican court finds three men guilty of 2024 killing of Australian, US surfers
data.description:
A Mexican judge on Friday found three men guilty of the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip to the state of Baja California, a source at the court told Reuters.

Jesus Gerardo Garcia, known as "El Kekas," and the co-defendants identified simply as Irineo Francisco "N" and Angel Jesus "N," were found guilty of aggravated homicide, violent robbery and vehicle theft by a Baja California court.

The prosecution had sought sentences of up to 150 years against the suspects. According to the same source at the state court, the sentence will be announced on October 16.

Brothers Callum, 33, and Jake Robinson, 30, and American Jack Carter Rhoad, 30, were camping and surfing near Punta San Jose, about 80 km (50 miles) south of Ensenada, when they were reported missing in late April 2024.

After a days-long search, aided by the FBI, their bodies were found on May 3 at the bottom of a well. The victims were each found with gunshot wounds in the head, authorities said.

Prosecutors said the accused had attempted to carjack the tourists, who were shot when they tried to resist. Their truck was later found burned nearby.

Martin and Debra Robinson, the Robinsons' parents, traveled from their hometown of Perth to attend the four-week trial. Rhoad's widowed fiancee, Natalie Weirtz, spoke via video call from the United States.

In November 2025 Gisell Silva, Garcia's then-girlfriend, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for her involvement in the case. The woman, who was 23 at the time, was arrested a few days after the bodies of the victims were found.

While the Ensenada area is considered relatively safe, Baja California ranks among Mexico’s most violent states. Following the killings, the US State Department urged Americans to reconsider travel to the state due to crime and kidnapping risks.
